notes: Feature 2 task format was rewritten to match feature_tasks/1.json top-level shape exactly: parent_feature, planning_status, notes, small_features.

Workflow Canvas Foundation is the Figma-like canvas foundation only. Actual AI node execution, provider calls, orchestration, generated asset creation, export rendering, and individual node functionality remain later feature scopes.

Toolbar planning must compose shadcn primitives instead of relying on a standalone toolbar registry item. The toolbar should let users drag different placeholder node types onto the canvas, switch interaction modes, control zoom/fit, open command actions, and expose keyboard-accessible tooltips.

Node planning must include reusable node UI design: title, type icon, status badge, compact body, input and output ports, selection state, disabled execution controls, and an inspector handoff. The controls must clearly label deferred functionality.

Port planning must treat input and output ports as first-class typed graph entities. Users should be able to freely connect compatible node ports, select edges, delete edges, and see edge/port states without triggering hidden execution.

Demo doc analysis from D:/kpop/docs/canvas-node-connections.md: the legacy app uses DOM plus SVG app.js ownership for wireState, connections, port events, SVG rendering, undo/redo, and persistence; React only reads snapshots through an adapter. This is weak for X-META because connection shape is only { fromId, toId }, ports are DOM classes, SVG is redrawn imperatively, edges are not first-class selectable records, and persistence is coupled to node HTML.

Feature 2 should improve on the demo by implementing typed React graph state, first-class node/port/edge records, selectable edges, deterministic reducer or store behavior, and structured persistence payloads that can later be saved through FastAPI.

shadcn evidence: corepack pnpm dlx shadcn@latest docs confirmed docs/examples/API links for command, resizable, sidebar, toggle-group, tooltip, tabs, menubar, context-menu, sheet, scroll-area, and separator.

Registry evidence: apps/web/components.json configures @uitripled, but shadcn registry search for toolbar from apps/web was blocked by @uitripled catalog parse errors requiring name and homepage; the same search found no standalone toolbar item, so the canvas toolbar should be composed from available primitives.
Architecture boundary remains: Web owns canvas UX and local draft graph state; FastAPI later owns durable workflow/project/task state; web must not call AI providers directly.

Feature 2 implementation completed on 2026-06-26 with a canvas-first /workspace route, typed graph reducer, first-class ports and edges, local structured snapshots, reusable placeholder node UI, stateful bottom toolbar controls, stale-port rejection, and honest deferred backend/AI execution labels.

User-requested visual revision changed /workspace to match the reference direction: the dark dotted canvas is the main theme, node creation lives behind one bottom Add node entry, the left node palette was removed to avoid duplicate add controls, and the right monitoring/Inspector panel was removed.

verification: Implement a canvas workspace route that reuses the existing app shell and opens on the production work surface rather than a marketing page.
Verify the shell includes regions for composed toolbar, canvas viewport, task/history signals, and honest unavailable-backend states.
Verify desktop behavior has no document overflow, text overlap, duplicated add controls, or right-side monitoring panel.

The route hides the global top bar on /workspace and renders a dark dotted canvas, floating workspace top bar, bottom toolbar, local-only draft status, and deferred backend/AI labels.

small_features.title: Composable Canvas Toolbar And Node Add Entry
small_features.user_visible_behavior: Users can add different node types from one bottom toolbar entry and use visible canvas controls.
verification: Plan and implement the toolbar as a composed control surface using shadcn primitives instead of a standalone toolbar component.
Verify users can add placeholder nodes for script, storyboard, character image, prop/asset, scene image, image composition, audio, video, and export from the bottom Add node menu.
Verify command, mode, zoom, fit, help, context, and panel toggles are keyboard-accessible and expose tooltips.

Users add placeholder node types from the single bottom Add node menu; toolbar controls expose select, move, fit, zoom, save, restore, delete, and help without duplicating a left node palette.

small_features.title: Typed React Graph State
small_features.user_visible_behavior: Users can add, move, select, and delete canvas nodes while the graph remains stable and predictable.
verification: Define typed React graph records for nodes, ports, edges, selection, viewport, draft status, and persistence snapshots.
Verify graph state supports add node, move node, select node, delete selection, pan, zoom, fit view, and restore from a structured payload.
Verify state behavior is deterministic through reducer, store, or hook tests.
small_features.notes: Implemented in apps/web/src/lib/workflow-canvas/graph.ts and apps/web/src/lib/workflow-canvas/types.ts. Tests cover deterministic add, move, select, delete, connect, save, and restore behavior without DOM-owned node HTML.

small_features.title: First-Class Ports And Free Connections
small_features.user_visible_behavior: Users can connect node input and output ports freely and see valid edge feedback on the canvas.
verification: Implement first-class input and output port records with ids, labels, data types, direction, compatibility metadata, and parent node references.
Verify users can start a connection from an output port, preview the edge, drop on a compatible input port, and reject invalid/self/duplicate connections with clear feedback.
Verify connections do not auto-run node functionality or hidden generation tasks.
small_features.notes: Implemented as typed port and edge records with sourceNodeId, sourcePortId, targetNodeId, targetPortId, dataType, status, and label. Invalid, self, and duplicate connections are rejected by reducer logic and never start generation.

small_features.title: Selectable Edge Rendering And Graph Editing
small_features.user_visible_behavior: Users can select, inspect, and delete connections just like nodes.
verification: Render edges as selectable graph objects with hover, selected, invalid, and disabled visual states.
Verify selecting an edge updates inspector state and keyboard delete removes the selected edge without disturbing unrelated nodes.
Verify moved or resized nodes keep edge endpoints aligned without imperative DOM-owned redraw state.
small_features.notes: Implemented state-driven SVG edge rendering with selectable hit paths, selected styling, compact in-canvas status handoff, and selected-edge deletion through reducer state.

small_features.title: Reusable Node UI Design
small_features.user_visible_behavior: Users can recognize node purpose, status, inputs, outputs, and deferred actions from a consistent node card design.
verification: Create reusable node UI patterns for all placeholder node types with header, icon, title, status badge, compact content, ports, selected/hover/focus states, and disabled action affordances.
Verify node UI is readable at common zoom levels and does not resize unpredictably when selected, hovered, or connected.
Verify actual script, image, audio, video, and export functionality is clearly deferred to later feature files.
small_features.notes: Implemented compact node cards with icon, title, id, status badge, description, stable port affordances, input/output counts, selected state, and disabled Generate later controls.

small_features.title: Structured Persistence Payloads And Save Restore Boundary
small_features.user_visible_behavior: Users can save and restore the canvas graph shape when backend persistence becomes available, with clear local draft and error states before then.
verification: Define structured graph snapshot payloads for nodes, ports, edges, viewport, selection, version, and project/workflow identifiers.
Verify local save/restore fixtures can round-trip the graph without serializing DOM HTML.
Verify the web layer labels missing FastAPI durable persistence honestly and never calls AI providers directly.
small_features.notes: Implemented structured WorkflowSnapshot payloads and local save/restore reducer behavior. The UI labels FastAPI durable persistence as unavailable and does not call model providers.
